    release: moina v0.1.34
    
    v0.1.34 releases the upload filename fix merged after v0.1.33. safeFilename
    kept the name the browser sent, stripping only path separators and control
    characters, so a JPEG uploaded as photo.png (an MP4 as clip.mov, a PNG as
    x.html) was stored under a name that disagreed with the mimeType the server
    had detected and went back out unchanged in the Content-Disposition of
    GET /api/v1/media/{mediaID}. filepath.Base also turns an empty name into
    ".", so the existing "image" fallback was unreachable and "." or ".." became
    the stored filename.
    
    safeFilename(header, mimeType) now normalises the extension against a
    package-level mediaFilenameExtensions table that maps 1:1 to the six MIME
    types uploadMedia accepts (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, WebM). A name whose
    extension already belongs to the detected type is kept as sent (case
    insensitive, jpeg and jpg both count as JPEG, so 사진.JPG survives); a
    missing or foreign extension is replaced (photo.png becomes photo.jpg,
    notes becomes notes.jpg, clip.mov becomes clip.mp4); an empty name, "." or
    ".." becomes image.jpg or video.mp4 by kind. The 200-rune truncation applies
    to the stem before the extension is appended, and the path and control
    character stripping is unchanged. Rows already stored keep their filename
    because migrations are additive, so the rule applies from new uploads on.
    api/openapi.yaml describes the rule on Media.filename; the 120 route
    contracts are unchanged, and the frontend only reads filename as a string.
    A unit test covers 19 cases and a PostgreSQL integration test drives the
    real New() server through the session cookie, CSRF and pgx with a multipart
    upload: a PNG sent as photo.jpg becomes photo.png, ".." becomes image.png
    and an MP4 sent as clip.mov becomes clip.mp4 in the response filename, in
    media_assets.filename and in Content-Disposition. Both tests failed on the
    previous code before the fix and pass after it. net/http reads a part with
    filename="" as a value rather than a file, so the empty-name case is covered

    identifier or the MCP switch is missing. The resource identifier is the
    explicit value, else the site base URL plus /mcp, else the request address.
    The new mcp_oauth.go serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and
    .../mcp without authentication as bare JSON with
    Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (404 while off), and the MCP 401 carries

name: Release offline image

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    name: Build and publish moina image
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - name: Checkout full history
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: e2e/package-lock.json

      - name: Validate release provenance and version
        env:
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          [[ "${RELEASE_VERSION}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]
          test "${RELEASE_VERSION}" = "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < VERSION)"
          test "$(git cat-file -t "refs/tags/${RELEASE_VERSION}")" = tag
          git fetch --no-tags origin main
          release_commit="$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${RELEASE_VERSION}^{commit}")"
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "${release_commit}" origin/main

      - name: Require successful CI for exact release commit
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          release_commit="$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${RELEASE_VERSION}^{commit}")"
          conclusion="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs?head_sha=${release_commit}&event=push&status=completed&per_page=100" \
            --jq 'first(.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == "CI")) | .conclusion // empty')"
          test "${conclusion}" = success || { printf '오류: release commit %s의 성공한 CI가 없습니다.\n' "${release_commit}" >&2; exit 1; }

      - name: Source checks
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          bash -n scripts/*.sh
          bash scripts/check-runtime-contract.sh
          node scripts/check-app-routes.mjs
          node scripts/check-openapi-routes.mjs
          node scripts/check-brand-colors.mjs
          MOINA_REQUIRE_SCREENSHOTS=1 node scripts/qa-pages.mjs

      - name: Build service image
        env:
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg VERSION="${RELEASE_VERSION}" \
            --build-arg VCS_REF="$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${RELEASE_VERSION}^{commit}")" \
            --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
            --tag "moina:${RELEASE_VERSION}" .

      - name: Runtime smoke with PostgreSQL
        env:
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          cleanup() {
            docker rm -f moina-release-app moina-release-postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            docker network rm moina-release >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          }
          trap cleanup EXIT
          docker network create moina-release >/dev/null
          docker run -d --name moina-release-postgres --network moina-release \
            -e POSTGRES_DB=moina -e POSTGRES_USER=moina -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=release-password \
            postgres:17-alpine@sha256:18cfe3ef5e6815560c98237d6216d1e5119702fb0f3894c8785dd58b8bbe5d73 >/dev/null
          # The official image briefly exposes its temporary init server before
          # restarting PostgreSQL. Wait for init completion and final readiness.
          for attempt in {1..60}; do
            if docker logs moina-release-postgres 2>&1 | grep -F 'PostgreSQL init process complete; ready for start up.' >/dev/null && \
              docker exec moina-release-postgres pg_isready -U moina -d moina >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
            if [[ "${attempt}" -eq 60 ]]; then docker logs moina-release-postgres; exit 1; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          docker run -d --name moina-release-app --network moina-release \
            -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8080 \
            --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=64m \
            --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
            -e MOINA_POSTGRES_DSN='postgres://moina:release-password@moina-release-postgres:5432/moina?sslmode=disable' \
            -e MOINA_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN=release-admin \
            -e MOINA_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=release-password-12345 \
            -e MOINA_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)" \
            "moina:${RELEASE_VERSION}" >/dev/null
          for attempt in {1..60}; do
            curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:18080/readyz >/dev/null && break
            if [[ "${attempt}" -eq 60 ]]; then docker logs moina-release-app; exit 1; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          bash scripts/qa-api-smoke.sh http://127.0.0.1:18080 release-admin release-password-12345 "${RELEASE_VERSION}"
          npm ci --prefix e2e
          npm --prefix e2e exec -- playwright install --with-deps chromium
          MOINA_E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18080 \
            MOINA_E2E_USERNAME=release-admin \
            MOINA_E2E_PASSWORD=release-password-12345 \
            MOINA_E2E_VERSION="${RELEASE_VERSION}" \
            npm test --prefix e2e

      - name: Package and verify offline image
        env:
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          bash scripts/package-image.sh "${RELEASE_VERSION}" dist
          bash scripts/verify-image-package.sh "dist/moina-${RELEASE_VERSION}.tar.gz" "moina:${RELEASE_VERSION}"

      - name: Create GitHub Release with one image asset
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -Eeuo pipefail
          archive="dist/moina-${RELEASE_VERSION}.tar.gz"
          sha256="$(sha256sum "${archive}" | cut -d ' ' -f 1)"
          notes="$(mktemp)"
          download_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
          trap 'rm -f -- "${notes}"; rm -rf -- "${download_dir}"' EXIT
          {
            printf '## MOINA 오프라인 이미지\n\n'
            printf -- '- 파일: `%s`\n' "$(basename "${archive}")"
            printf -- '- 이미지: `moina:%s`\n' "${RELEASE_VERSION}"
            printf -- '- 플랫폼: `linux/amd64`\n'
            printf -- '- SHA256: `%s`\n\n' "${sha256}"

    release: moina v0.1.34
    
    v0.1.34 releases the upload filename fix merged after v0.1.33. safeFilename
    kept the name the browser sent, stripping only path separators and control
    characters, so a JPEG uploaded as photo.png (an MP4 as clip.mov, a PNG as
    x.html) was stored under a name that disagreed with the mimeType the server
    had detected and went back out unchanged in the Content-Disposition of
    GET /api/v1/media/{mediaID}. filepath.Base also turns an empty name into
    ".", so the existing "image" fallback was unreachable and "." or ".." became
    the stored filename.
    
    safeFilename(header, mimeType) now normalises the extension against a
    package-level mediaFilenameExtensions table that maps 1:1 to the six MIME
    types uploadMedia accepts (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, WebM). A name whose
    extension already belongs to the detected type is kept as sent (case
    insensitive, jpeg and jpg both count as JPEG, so 사진.JPG survives); a
    missing or foreign extension is replaced (photo.png becomes photo.jpg,
    notes becomes notes.jpg, clip.mov becomes clip.mp4); an empty name, "." or
    ".." becomes image.jpg or video.mp4 by kind. The 200-rune truncation applies
    to the stem before the extension is appended, and the path and control
    character stripping is unchanged. Rows already stored keep their filename
    because migrations are additive, so the rule applies from new uploads on.
    api/openapi.yaml describes the rule on Media.filename; the 120 route
    contracts are unchanged, and the frontend only reads filename as a string.
    A unit test covers 19 cases and a PostgreSQL integration test drives the
    real New() server through the session cookie, CSRF and pgx with a multipart
    upload: a PNG sent as photo.jpg becomes photo.png, ".." becomes image.png
    and an MP4 sent as clip.mov becomes clip.mp4 in the response filename, in
    media_assets.filename and in Content-Disposition. Both tests failed on the
    previous code before the fix and pass after it. net/http reads a part with
    filename="" as a value rather than a file, so the empty-name case is covered
    by the unit test only.
    
    This commit itself carries only the version bump: VERSION, the OpenAPI info
    block, the package manifests and their lockfiles, the SPA fallback version,
    the Dockerfile build args, the OG card and the screenshot manifest, plus the
    version strings the published docs, the Markdown guides and READMEs quote.
    The PDF prints of the two guides are left as they are because the repository
    carries no tool to regenerate them. The README release paragraph now names
    the upload filename extension normalisation.

    throwaway PostgreSQL (38 integration tests) and go vet across the backend,
    staticcheck clean, and the frontend at 250 passing tests, ESLint within its
    40 warning budget, and a v0.1.34 production build.
